pattern.crimePattern: operations manager paid by a shell company kills the documentation clerk who refused to pass blank title-deed paper as printing paper; staged as a fall
pattern.notes: Fictional freight station, clearing agency, container number and shell company. No real port operator, customs officer or registry is shown doing wrong. Spine boss case.

ob.text: The security office of Bandari Freight Station, Shimanzi, reports that documentation clerk Naomi Chepkemoi (38), of Pwani Clearing & Forwarding, was found at the foot of an external staircase. Recorded by the company as an accidental fall at about 06:00. Her phone is missing.

facts.text: Documentation clerk Naomi Chepkemoi was found at the foot of the external staircase at Bandari Freight Station. The company recorded an accidental fall at about 06:00.
Her phone is missing.
Head injuries at the foot of the stairs. Her ID lanyard and gate card are on her.
Company security report: 'Fell from the external staircase on arrival for the 06:00 shift. Accident.' Approved by D. Gichuru. The owner, Yusuf Mazrui, accepted it within the hour.
Gate log: 'N. Chepkemoi — in 22:40 (night cut-off shift) — no exit.' She never left, and never arrived at 06:00.
Gate log: 'D. Gichuru, car KDB xxx — in 23:05 — out 23:50.' No other movements 22:45–00:30 except the night operators already inside.
Ramadhan: at about 23:35 he heard a woman cry out from the office block. Gichuru drove out at 23:50, "fast, without greeting me".
Ramadhan: last week the stacker operator, Samson Odera, shouted at Naomi about his overtime sign-offs.
Ramadhan: Fatma Ruwa, the other clerk, wanted Naomi's senior post. "Everybody knew."
Ramadhan: "People say Naomi lent the boss money. I don't know."
Ramadhan was at the gate all night; the log has an entry in his hand every fifteen minutes.
Naomi to her sister, 23:12: 'Gichuru amekuja. Anataka nisaini PCFU kama printing paper. Si printing paper. Ona.' (Gichuru's here, wants me to sign PCFU as printing paper. It isn't. Look.) Photo.
Container PCFU 418220-3: 'printing paper, A3, 40 cartons'. Consignee: Mvua Holdings Ltd, Nairobi. The customs entry is unsigned by the documentation clerk.
Inside PCFU 418220-3: watermarked security paper with fibres, not printing paper. One carton opened and resealed with fresh tape.
On every sheet, an empty printed oval: 'Registrar's seal here'. Blank title-deed paper.
Records, Naomi's line: Shimanzi mast until 23:52, then Nyali 00:05–00:20, then off.
Records, Gichuru's line: Shimanzi 23:00–23:52, Nyali (his home zone) from 00:05.
PesaPap, Gichuru's line: monthly B2C payments from MVUA HOLDINGS LTD, KSh 120,000 each, for 14 months.
PesaPap, Gichuru's line: no transactions of any kind with Naomi.
Yard tally: Samson Odera's reach-stacker moves at 23:10, 23:20, 23:34, 23:41 and 23:58, all at the far end of the yard.
Vessel tally: Fatma Ruwa tallying on board at berth from 23:00 to 03:00, signing every half hour.
Mazrui's house guard: he was home in Nyali all night.
On Mazrui's desk: a revenue-authority audit notice about tax rates on storage fees. Nothing to do with Naomi or Gichuru. It explains why he wanted no police at the yard.
Odera's overtime sheets: all signed by Naomi on Friday. The dispute was settled.
Gichuru's drawer, 'Mvua — movements': 'PCFU 418220-3 — Nairobi by road.'
Same list, older line: 'Lamu by dhow — Upepo Mwema — captain refused.'
Same list, last line: 'Bahati — old matter — closed 12 yrs.'
Gichuru: "I was home in Nyali all night. I heard about Naomi this morning like everyone else."
Gichuru: "That container is printing paper. I've seen the invoice."
Gichuru admits he drove in at 23:05 "to collect a file" from his office upstairs. He says he didn't see Naomi.
Gichuru: "I don't open cartons. I sign what I'm given."
Gichuru: he was recruited by "a man with a bad leg they call Fundi", who brings the cash and never uses a phone. He has never heard the name Kivuli.
Odera: "I was on the stacker all night."
Fatma: "I was on the ship until three."
Fatma: "I wanted her job. I didn't want her dead." The senior clerk's post is a clerk's post, not the manager's.
Mazrui: "My security said she fell. I believed them."
Gladys is in Eldoret; she got the message there and called Naomi's phone all night.

interrogations.intro: Gichuru receives Amani in his office with tea already poured. "A tragedy. Eight years with us. Those stairs are steep in the dark."

topics.reply: Our security people are very thorough. A fall. I approved it this morning.
A long silence. Then: "A man with a bad leg. They call him Fundi. He brings cash. He never uses a phone. I don't know any other name. I want a lawyer."

interrogations.intro: Odera climbs down from his stacker cab and keeps his hard hat on. "I didn't go near the office block."

topics.reply: She signed my overtime on Friday. All of it. She was fair. I shouted at her last week and she was still fair.

interrogations.intro: Fatma answers from a ship's deck, gulls and a crane horn behind her. "Naomi? Naomi?"

topics.reply: I wanted her job. I didn't want her dead. And it was her job I wanted, not his.

interrogations.intro: Mazrui meets Amani at the gate and doesn't invite him in. "My security said she fell. I believed them."

topics.reply: Yes. I didn't want police in my yard. For my own reasons. Not hers. Look at the notice; it is about storage fees.

interrogations.intro: Gladys, from Eldoret, has the message open before Amani asks. "She sent me this. Look at it. Look at what she sent me."
Ramadhan holds the gate log open with both thumbs. "I write everybody. Every quarter of an hour. Everybody."

topics.reply: Odera? He was on his stacker at the far end all night. I could hear it.

contradictions.reaction: I came to collect a file. From my office. Twenty minutes. I didn't see her. I didn't even know she was on shift.
I don't open cartons. I sign what I'm given. The invoice says paper. Paper is paper.

proof.concludes: Naomi came in at 22:40 for the night cut-off and never left. The report's "06:00, on arrival" is false. The accident story is wrong from the start.
At 23:12 Naomi refused to sign PCFU 418220-3 as printing paper. It is title-deed security paper, consigned to Mvua Holdings, and Gichuru was pressing her.
Gichuru wasn't home. He drove in at 23:05 and out at 23:50, fifteen minutes after the cry. Pressed, he admits being upstairs.

Naomi's phone left Shimanzi at 23:52 and went to Nyali, exactly as Gichuru's did. Mvua Holdings has paid him every month for fourteen months. Daniel Gichuru killed her because she wouldn't pass Mvua's paper.
The empty oval on the paper is waiting for a REGISTRAR OF TITLES seal. The only seal on the Pattern File is the one Mvua ordered from Rashid Omar in case 10.

The overtime dispute was Odera's, and it was settled on Friday.

There are no transactions between them at all.

reconstruction.text: Container PCFU 418220-3 arrives declared as printing paper, consigned to Mvua Holdings. Naomi opens a carton for the sample check. Watermarks, fibres, and an empty oval: "Registrar's seal here".
She photographs a sheet, keeps one, and won't sign the entry. She is working the night cut-off for a vessel.
23:05. Gichuru drives in. Sign it, he says, and names a sum. 23:12: she messages her sister, "It's not printing paper. Look."
About 23:35, on the outside staircase, he grabs for the sample sheet and her phone. She falls. He goes down after her.
23:50. He drives out with her phone and the sheet. In the morning his security man types up a fall at 06:00.

afterVerdict.beat: Interview room. Gichuru was recruited by "a man with a bad leg they call Fundi", who brings the cash and never uses a phone. He has never heard the name Kivuli. He asks for a lawyer.

The drawer list goes to the Pattern File: the container's route (t_mvua); "Lamu by dhow — Upepo Mwema — captain refused", which quietly explains one more thing Khamis said no to in case 24 (Ireri had nothing to do with Mvua); and "Bahati — old matter — closed 12 yrs".
Joseph Mwenda died outside Nakuru twelve years ago. When the Bahati pin lands, the desk lamp dims for a beat. Nothing is said.
The container is seized. Its paper goes to the evidence store in Nairobi.
Collectible: a brass dhow compass from Lamu, with a note from Abdalla Khamis: "Baba refused them too. Thank you for reading him right."
